description:
Apply a pseudocolor (color ramp) symbology to a grayscale elevation raster in gvSIG Desktop.

gvSIG Desktop is open. A grayscale raster file is available at `/home/ga/gvsig_data/elevation.tif`.

Your task:
1. Add the raster layer `/home/ga/gvsig_data/elevation.tif` to the View. It will appear in black and white (grayscale) by default.
2. Open the 'Layer Properties' for this raster layer (Right-click layer > Properties).
3. Navigate to the 'Bands' or 'Color Table' tab (depending on the raster driver, usually under the 'Bands' tab -> 'Color Table' or 'Symbology').
4. Enable/Apply a Color Table (Color Ramp) such as 'Rainbow', 'Relief', or 'Precipitation' so the raster displays with multiple colors based on pixel values.
5. Ensure the map view shows the colorful raster.
6. Export the current View as a PNG image to `/home/ga/gvsig_data/exports/colored_elevation.png`.

Note: The export must show the raster with a color ramp applied, not just grayscale.
